In detail

No dated safety-specific press coverage was found for this quartier, which covers the canal Saint-Martin (quai de Valmy/quai de Jemmapes) and the hospital grounds. This is a popular, largely gentrified picnic-and-nightlife strip; the only relevant context is the ordinary crowd/noise of canal-side bars on warm evenings, not a documented crime problem.

Frequently asked questions

Is Hôpital-Saint-Louis (10e arr.) safe?

Hôpital-Saint-Louis (10e arr.) was reviewed at area level and no traveller-relevant safety concern was documented for it in the sources checked. Wandroz records that as no findings, not as a safety rating: an absence of reporting is not evidence that an area is safe. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Paris publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Why does Hôpital-Saint-Louis (10e arr.) have no rating?

Because the review found nothing to rate it on. Areas with documented, sourced signals get a level; areas without them are shown as reviewed with no findings, so you can tell the difference between an area that was checked and came back clear of documented issues and one that was never looked at. Both are treated as inconclusive here rather than as reassurance.

Is Hôpital-Saint-Louis (10e arr.) a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Nothing documented argues against it, and nothing documented argues for it either. For a stay, weigh it against the rated areas on the Paris map and check recent reviews for the specific street. You can search accommodation already scoped to this area using the Booking.com link on this page.
